## Skillerr 0.1.5

**Trails: pick up where you left off**
- Skillerr now learns what you're working on from how you browse. Pages you visit are filed into trails like
  "Kyoto ryokan near Gion", by what they were opened from, what you searched and what they're about.
- Trails notice what you left unfinished: a form you typed into but never sent, an article you read partway, a cart you
  didn't check out, a long video you stopped halfway.
- **Tidy** in the tab strip keeps the 5 tabs you're using and tucks the rest into their trails. Tabs you haven't used
  for 12 hours are tucked on their own once you have 9 or more open. Undo brings them all back.
- Tucked tabs stay in sight: each trail sits at the start of the tab strip with its tabs' icons. Click it and its tabs
  unfold right there; click one to open it again.
- The start page shows **Pick up where you left off**. **Continue** reopens a trail's tabs, or the page you stopped at,
  scrolled to where you were. Quitting no longer loses your tabs: **Reopen all** brings them back.
- ⋮ → **Trails**: rename, merge, mark done, forget, never learn from a site, and start from your Chrome history.
- AI apps can see your trails (`my_trails`, `continue_trail`) only after you allow each one once.
- Everything stays on your computer. Trails never keep page text or what you typed. Turn them off in Settings.

**History: everything you and your AIs looked into**
- ⌘Y opens **History**: one map with Kilr glowing at the centre and everything you and your AI apps looked into
  coming out of it as threads of light. Your pages are warm colours, your AIs' cool ones (one per app), and pages you
  both opened are green. Kilr burns brighter as your history grows. Filter to yours or your AIs', or search by meaning.
- Click Kilr to see what it's doing on your computer: its size, the memory it uses, how fast it is, what it has
  learned, and a live log of what it just did. Runs on your CPU, no GPU needed, works offline.
- The old list of visited pages and bookmarks is now **Bookmarks & Data**.

**Kilr: Skillerr's own small AI**
- Built in: one 8 MB file, fast enough to read every page title as you browse. Runs on your CPU, no GPU needed, and
  nothing leaves your computer.
- **Suggests skills from what you keep doing.** When you (or your AIs) do the same kind of task again and again, like
  choosing what to buy with the same searches and review sites, Kilr offers to save how you do it as a skill any AI
  can use. It's worked out from your trails; no AI model writes it.
- Pages join the right trail even when they're worded differently, and **Ask Kilr** on the Trails page finds a trail
  by what you mean ("plane tickets to Japan" finds your Tokyo flights).
- The start page says where you were and what you didn't finish.
- Recall by meaning now works out of the box, without Ollama.
- **Your tabs sort themselves** into named trail groups in the tab strip. Focus on one trail, or put a trail's tabs
  away, with one click.
- **Find anything by meaning** from the address bar: type what you remember, and open, tucked and visited pages
  appear. Enter brings one back where you were.
- **Kilr learns your words, and your AIs'** every week, on your computer, in under a second, and keeps what it learned
  only if it files your pages better. Choose when, and whether it learns from your browsing, your AIs' research or
  both, in Trails → Settings.
- **Tidy** also closes duplicate tabs.
- **Move over from Chrome:** your open Chrome tabs come over sorted into trails (Settings → Bring your Chrome data).
- **Research your AI does** (Claude Desktop, Cursor…) becomes its own trail, named after what it was researching, that
  you can continue later.
- The live view inside your AI app's chat shows the Skillerr wheel, spinning while your AI drives, and sharper tab
  thumbnails that no longer cut off the page's edges.
- Fixed: an AI's `fetch_page` could read a blank page instead of the one it asked for.

**Install:** `curl -fsSL https://skillerr.com/install.sh | sh` (macOS, Linux) or `irm https://skillerr.com/install.ps1 | iex`
(Windows). Installed copies on Windows, the Linux AppImage and signed Mac builds update themselves.
